testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for these problems: cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube used to move air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made by air brakes when used
A part within the braking unit that allows air to move freely

questions.correctAnswerText: A type of warning system
questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: In bad weather, many drivers:

options.text: Like to drive in front of trucks
Like to be on the side of trucks
Like to drive without using their lights

questions.correctAnswerText: Like to follow trucks
questions.explanation: In bad weather with poor visibility, many drivers follow closely behind trucks. If someone is tailgating you, increase the distance between your vehicle and theirs.

questions.question: If you're not sure how to handle a fire, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the firefighters
questions.explanation: If you are unsure how to put out a fire, wait for firefighters to arrive. Let them handle it, especially with hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: What should happen if air pressure in the brake system falls below 60 psi?

options.text: The warning light will come on
The vehicle will not shift out of gear
The steering wheel will lock up

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light will come on
questions.explanation: On vehicles with air brakes, a warning light comes on if pressure falls below 60 psi. On large buses, the warning may activate at 80 to 85 psi.

questions.question: On newer vehicles, how do you set the parking brake?

options.text: Move a lever to the right
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob
Pull up on the steering column

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob to set the parking brake. Push it in to release the brake.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane. Driving tired is dangerous.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a cause for concern
Is not a concern if passengers are not unloading
Should not be on the roadway
Is a concern, whether passengers are visible or not

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern, whether passengers are visible or not
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind it, and the bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will prevent the turn signals from working
Pose no threat if the vehicle is only driven on highways

questions.correctAnswerText: Indicate a potentially dangerous defect
questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps axles in place. Damaged suspension parts like leaking shock absorbers can be dangerous defects.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Plan ahead for dangerous situations that could happen
Focus only on your own driving and ignore other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead for dangerous situations that could happen
questions.explanation: While driving, check the road ahead for hazards. Develop a plan to handle any dangerous situations that might occur.

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.correctAnswerText: Water and oil
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These substances can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: To leave a stop safely, you should park:

options.text: So that you must back up to leave your parking space.
So that you can pull forward to leave your parking space.
On the side of a roadway, not in a parking lot.
By backing into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So that you can pull forward to leave your parking space.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous. When possible, park so you can pull forward to exit instead of backing up.

questions.question: When trying to avoid a hazard:

options.text: Swerving may be more effective than stopping.
You may change lanes without looking.
You should drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be more effective than stopping.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best choice. You can turn away from a hazard faster than you can stop. However, swerving can be risky for top-heavy vehicles or vehicles pulling trailers, as they may roll over.

questions.question: What is sleep debt?

options.text: When you fall behind on sleep
When you want to take a nap
The amount of time it takes to get ready to drive after sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: When you fall behind on sleep
questions.explanation: Sleep debt builds up when you do not get enough sleep. You can only pay back this debt by getting more sleep.

questions.question: A registered vehicle should have:

options.text: A mirror on the left side only.
Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
A mirror on the right side only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mirrors on both the left and right sides.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires knowing what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Your vehicle should have mirrors on both sides, and you should check them regularly.

questions.question: Bent lock rings:

options.text: Are not a concern in dry weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are dangerous.
questions.explanation: Bent, cracked, or mismatched lock rings are dangerous and should not be used.

questions.question: Laws about securing loads and vehicle weights vary by state. During interstate travel:

options.text: The law of the state in which the trip originated takes precedence.
The law of the state the vehicle is in takes precedence.
The driver should request federal regulations to override conflicting state laws.
The driver can choose which state's laws to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The law of the state the vehicle is in takes precedence.
questions.explanation: Vehicle weight, cargo securement, load covering, and where large vehicles can drive are controlled by federal, state, and local laws. These rules differ by location. The state laws where you are driving apply to you.

questions.question: Which of the following could reduce the space between the road and an overhead object, like a bridge?
questions.correctAnswerText: A repaving of the road
questions.explanation: Do not assume that bridge height signs are exactly correct. If the road was repaved after the sign was installed, or if there is snow on the ground, the clearance may be different from what the sign shows.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a distracted person that motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful around people not paying attention to the road. Watch for drivers talking with passengers, children near the road, and road workers.

questions.question: Alcohol is removed from the body:

options.text: At a rate that changes depending on how much alcohol is in the body.
At a consistent rate, regardless of how much alcohol is in the body.
More quickly if the person drinks coffee.
More quickly if the person stays awake.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a consistent rate, regardless of how much alcohol is in the body.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate that cannot be sped up by drinking coffee or taking a cold shower. The only way to sober up is to wait for your body to process the alcohol out of your system.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
One minute after you hit the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The distance you can see ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop your vehicle within the area you can see on the road ahead. Slow down when you cannot see far enough due to weather, darkness, or other conditions.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in the car
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not pay attention to the road. Children may run into the road without looking. Be careful around construction workers. A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus is not a driving concern.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Use flashing lights so other drivers move out of your way.
Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and arrive when you arrive.
questions.explanation: Do not drive dangerously or aggressively. Stay calm and accept delays. Plan your trip early to avoid rushing and stress.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, pressure of at least ____ should be built up in both brake systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before you drive, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary brake systems.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: Usually thick — about half an inch or more.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually thin.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like the road is just wet.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get enough sleep before you drive
Schedule trips during hours when you would normally be sleeping

questions.correctAnswerText: Schedule trips during hours when you would normally be sleeping
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is very dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before driving. Have another driver ride with you. Drive during hours when you are normally awake. Avoid medicines that make you sleepy.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly many times.
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly many times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work correctly. After the system fills with air, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal many times. The warning light should come on when the pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Why do you need to drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be drained
To allow air pressure to change

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be drained
questions.explanation: Compressed air in the brake system contains water and oil. If left in the system, they can damage the brakes. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep per night does an adult need to stay alert?
questions.correctAnswerText: Eight to nine
questions.explanation: Getting enough rest is important for safe driving. Most people need eight to nine hours of sleep per night to stay alert and focused.

questions.question: Too little weight on a steering axle can result in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Poor traction.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be balanced so the vehicle handles safely. If cargo is too far back, the front axle becomes too light. The front wheels will not have enough grip, and steering will become unsafe.

questions.question: Why are roads slippery when it first starts to rain?

options.text: Rain mixes with oil on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first falls, it mixes with oil and grease already on the road. This creates a slippery film. As more rain falls, this mixture washes away.

questions.question: How should you use stab braking in an emergency?

options.text: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
Press the brakes halfway while keeping the wheels rolling.
Press the brakes fully, lock the wheels, and hold until the vehicle stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes fully until the wheels lock. Release until the wheels roll again. Repeat this process.
questions.explanation: Stab braking means pressing the brakes all the way until the wheels lock. Then release the brakes so the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process to stop safely.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It only happens when you do something physical, like use a cell phone.
It can happen from thinking about other things, like daydreaming.
It is fine on empty roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen from thinking about other things, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Mental distractions are just as dangerous as physical ones. You might look at a hazard but not notice it if your mind is thinking about something else.

questions.question: While driving downhill, you should brake until your speed is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake.
questions.correctAnswerText: 5 mph
questions.explanation: When going downhill, brake until you reach a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle can fit under a bridge, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely under a bridge, slow down. Try to find another route if possible.

questions.question: Where must a dolly with ABS have its malfunction lamp?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side
questions.explanation: A dolly with Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) must have a yellow malfunction lamp on the left side.

questions.question: If you must drive very slowly, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, if your local laws allow it.

questions.question: During an inspection, your brake pads should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Check brake pads for problems like cracked drums, and pads covered in oil, grease, or brake fluid. Also check for missing, broken, or very worn pads.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and traffic first.
Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow instructions.
Refuse to change lanes if you don't want to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and traffic first.
questions.explanation: You will need to change lanes multiple times during the driving test. Always check traffic first and use proper signals. Change lanes smoothly when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Not use four-way flashers because this is a test, not an emergency.
Leave the vehicle in first gear.
Park in front of a fire hydrant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop for the stop/start maneuver during the driving test, turn on your four-way flashers and shift into neutral or park. Do not block driveways, intersections, fire hydrants, or signs.

questions.question: How can you prevent your tires and engine from overheating in hot weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the hotter your engine and tires become. In hot weather, driving slower helps prevent overheating.

questions.question: When can brakes get out of adjustment?

options.text: If they are used at all.
If one side is used more than the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: If they are hot.
questions.explanation: Hot brakes are likely to get out of adjustment. Use proper braking techniques to keep your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, what may be needed?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the engine running.
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require the engine to be running when you check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: How can you avoid being blinded by bright headlights at night?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights at night, look to the right edge of the road until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during a vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of a trailer load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: In S-cam brakes, what does the air pressure move when you press the brake pedal?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slack adjuster.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters. This twists the brake camshafts.

questions.question: During an inspection, lug nuts should be all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: During inspection, lug nuts must be present, free of cracks and damage, and tight. They should not be loose. Check that all bolt holes are also free of cracks and damage.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do?

options.text: Makes a vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes handling a vehicle harder.
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle harder to handle and less safe to drive.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the pedal.
The distance between the brake pedal's resting spot and the floor.
The amount of air pressure used to stop a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the pedal.
questions.explanation: Air takes time to travel through brake lines. With air brakes, there is usually at least a half-second delay between pressing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work. Hydraulic brakes work instantly.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum loaded weight of a vehicle stated by the manufacturer.
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a vehicle can carry.
The maximum weight allowed on a single trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum loaded weight of a vehicle stated by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: GVWR is the maximum weight that a vehicle and its load can weigh together, as stated by the manufacturer.
